name: Duroliponte
type: castrum; ancient Roman structure; Roman colony; Roman city
text: Duroliponte or Durolipons was a small town in the Roman province of Britannia on the site of what is now the city of Cambridge. The site of Roman Cambridge is located on Castle Hill, just northwest of the city centre. The fort (Latin: castrum) was bounded on two sides by the lines formed by the present Mount Pleasant, continuing across Huntingdon Road into Clare Street.

depictions.name: Duroliponte
depictions.text: Duroliponte was a former Roman fortified town in Cambridgeshire, whose site later became the city of Cambridge. In 873, a group of Vikings of the Great Summer Army under Soma sought refuge at the fort after being driven out by the Anglo-Saxons led by Wigmund. Led by Magni, the Vikings were found by Eivor Varinsdottir of the Raven Clan, who sought an alliance with Soma's clan.
